applicationChunkerSource.executionCaveat: The container bind-mounted apps/server/src read-only. runtime-provenance.json hashes the executor but does not list this imported chunker module separately; the module hash above is the matching clean source at the bind-mounted path.

testHarness.memorySource: The harness records totalMs with performance.now() and memoryPeakBytes from /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak (line 104). This is whole-container cgroup high-water, not per-process or per-operator memory.

genesisrag17ChunkerConfiguration.maxTokensMeaning: Whitespace tokens matched by /\S+/u in chunker code, not multilingual-E5 tokenizer tokens.
genesisrag17ChunkerConfiguration.boundaryPolicy: NFKC-bounded character window, whitespace-token cap, preferred text boundaries, and grapheme-safe boundaries; whichever cap is reached first ends a window.
sourceReferences: native.test.js:25-47 (prepared text arm is passed to the GenesisRAG17 TEXT ingestion provider without a maxTokens override)

embeddingCallPattern.textsPerPassageCall: All decision chunks, in order; no microbatch loop or batch-size cap in the pinned worker/sidecar.
embeddingCallPattern.tokenizerCall: Tokenizer.encode_batch over the full passage list, with truncation at 512 tokens.
embeddingCallPattern.padding: Every text in that call is padded to the longest encoded text in the same batch (dynamic max length), rather than padded independently.
embeddingCallPattern.additionalEmbeddings: Retrieval/query embeddings are separate single-query calls in the native index/benchmark stage; measured Stage 16 is 1.57s baseline versus 1.67s combined, so it does not explain the Stage 15 increase.
embeddingCallPattern.freshRunBehavior: Each arm has a fresh worker/container and isolated store; all passage vectors are recomputed for that arm. Model artifact hash verification and Python tokenizer/ONNX session initialization occur once per worker inside Stage 15 before its passage batch.

inputMounts: the pinned model-volume tokenizer.json, mounted read-only
tokenizerOnlyShapeDiagnostic.method: Python 3.12.15 / tokenizers 0.23.1 loaded the exact pinned tokenizer.json, enabled max_length=512 truncation, and encoded passage: + each raw chunk text. No ONNX session was created and no session.run was called.

prefixCheck.note: The entire prior prefix is encoded again in the combined run. Its 277 chunks are byte-identical, but all share the new batch max length of 269 instead of 225.

fixed32PredictedShapeOnly.caveat: The tensor estimates use BERT dimensions and theoretical tensor shapes. ONNX graph fusion, memory planning, and arena reuse were not profiled; these figures are not measured RSS or cgroup allocations. Ten sequential ORT calls may change wall time, and no performance result is claimed here.

interpretation.supportedConclusion: The large timing increase is concentrated in Stage 15, while Stage 16 remains about 1.6-2.1s. The pinned path runs a single dynamically padded CPU batch, and the combined batch increases the max sequence length from 225 to 269 while adding 25 chunks; this repads and recomputes the identical 277-chunk prefix. The batch/token shape is a credible mechanism for superlinear compute and activation growth beyond vector count.
interpretation.notProven: The historical runs are not paired repeats. Stage 15 includes model artifact hashing and worker/session startup as well as tokenization and inference. Cgroup memory is a whole-container high-water mark. No ONNX operator profile or fresh same-time control was captured, so the full elapsed or 1.68GiB peak delta cannot be assigned to a specific operator or tensor from these receipts alone.
